title: An observational, non-interventional, multicenter, prospective study to explore the association of MS-related disability worsening and loss of thalamus volume
summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the extent to which multiple sclerosis (MS)-related brain matter damage is associated with an increase in disability and whether a further increase in disability can be predicted in the presence of brain matter impairment. A total of 600 patients with relapsing-remitting MS at 20 clinics/practices will participate in the study. Only data from your routine treatment will be collected and evaluated as part of the study. We would like to use and evaluate the data collected in the course of routine treatment for our study over 36 months. This will be the following data: MRI data and data on the degree of MS-related disability (EDSS).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
General
● MS, as diagnosed by the revised 2017 McDonald criteria
● Ages 18 to 55 years, inclusive

Active MS (arm 1)
● Meet one of the following disease activity criteria
a. more than 10 T2 lesions at the time of the first visit OR
b. at least one documented relapse with the last 12 months prior to the first visit OR
c. documented evidence of at least 1 Gd-enhancing lesion on brain MRI within the last 12 months prior to the first visit OR
d. documented evidence of at least one new or one enlarging T2 lesion within the last 12 months prior to the first visit.
● Either receive or about to receive oral immune therapies as first or second DMT approach, such as teriflunomide, ozanimod, dimethylfumarate, ponesimod, and diroximethylfumarate.
● Either receive or about to receive second line therapies, such as e.g. monoclonal antibodies, but the number of patients receiving monoclonal antibodies should be restricted to 1/3 of the overall study population.

Progredient MS (arm 2)
● No relapses in the last two years and with progressive disease features as defined by clinical (disability worsening) or imaging (abnormal whole brain volume loss) 
● Patients initially enrolled in the first arm (active MS patients) may be switched to the second arm (progressive MS patients) during the course of the study if, at a scheduled visit, they are found to meet the criteria of the second arm.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who are not eligible to receive MRI
